thread:
Devon: heads up — support is getting a handful of reports about elevated 429s and a few billing spikes after yesterday's quota rollforward. customers mostly on the mid-tier plans. I can see errors in the gateway logs around quota checks failing with a key mismatch.

Ashley: thanks — which rollout are we talking about? the staged limit bump for better burst handling?

Devon: yeah, the staged quota increase we pushed at 03:30UTC (feature-flag:quota-bump-v2). rollout was set to 20% per region, but we saw an unexpected jump to ~60% in eu-west.

Marta: adding logs from the gateway:```
[2026-03-15T03:31:12Z] tenant=acme svc=quota-check status=500 err="quota-meta-parse-failed" details="expected v2 schema, got v1"
[2026-03-15T03:31:12Z] tenant=acme svc=auth status=200 token=ok
[2026-03-15T03:31:12Z] tenant=acme svc=rate-limiter action=reject code=429 key=tenant:acme:burst
```
Looks like some control plane metadata didn't migrate for a subset of tenants, fallback path mis-evaluates and we end up double-applying a stricter quota.

Support-Lead: customer-facing summary: "We're investigating intermittent 429s affecting bursts after capacity config changes. If you see 'quota-meta-parse-failed' in logs, please DM with your tenant ID."

Matt: I'm on rollback if we need it. What's the safe rollback plan? Do we flip the feature flag off or revert control-plane state?

Devon: short term: toggle feature-flag quota-bump-v2 -> off. That should route everyone to the stable v1 codepath. Longer term we need to reconcile control-plane metadata for affected tenants.

Marta: quick check: I can run this query to list affected tenants and whether they have the v2 schema bit set:```sql
SELECT tenant_id, quota_schema_version FROM tenant_quota_meta WHERE quota_schema_version != 'v2' AND last_updated > '2026-03-15';
```
I'll patch/queue any missing conversions.

SRE-Bot: deploy-bot: feature-flag quota-bump-v2 toggled OFF by Marta at 03:42 UTC — rollout aborted. New traffic distribution: stable=100%

Ashley: good. support, please keep the customer messages templated: short, avoid technical details. I'll update the status page and add an incident note.

Support-Lead: updated status page: "Partial 429s observed for burst traffic in EU region after quota configuration change. We reverted the staged change and are reconciling tenant quota metadata. No data loss. ETA for full resolution: 2-4 hours for validation."

Matt: after flag flip, are we seeing errors drop?

Marta: metrics trending: 429 rate in eu-west fell from ~1.8% of requests to 0.06% within 4 minutes of toggle. There are a few stragglers tied to cached policy shards. Running a cache invalidation job now:```bash
./tools/policy-cache-invalidate --region eu-west --shard 12 --reason "post-rollback reconcile"
```

Devon: good to see recovery. Action items: 1) Marta to run conversion for tenants missing v2 metadata and validate against canary tenant list (don't push new flag until confident). 2) Matt to prepare a staged rollforward playbook: include health-check endpoints, a stricter per-region ramp (5% -> 10% -> 25%), and explicit preflight query that verifies quota-schema for a random sample. 3) Ashley to coordinate customer comms and postmortem.

Support-Lead: customer triage — collect tenant IDs and timestamp ranges for affected requests and escalate any billing anomalies to finance.

Marta: started conversion job for 42 tenants flagged by the query. I'll post updates in this thread as each batch finishes.

Devon: reminder for postmortem: include why metadata migration wasn't enforced during the initial rollout and add a step to block rollouts if tenant metadata scan fails.

Matt: also recommend adding an automated smoke test that simulates burst traffic and validates no 429s for a canary tenant after toggling the flag. I'll draft the test case.

SRE-Bot: incident-note: 1930012468 - staged quota rollforward triggered elevated 429s for burst traffic. Mitigated by toggling feature-flag and running tenant metadata reconcile. Follow-up required: rollout playbook + metadata validation.

Devon: thanks everyone. keeping this thread open until conversions complete and we've validated a safe rollforward path. If numbers look stable by +4h we'll close and schedule a postmortem write-up. :white_check_mark:
